newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: QUICK VIEW - ING NINE MONTH RESULTS.
newsitem.headline: QUICK VIEW - ING NINE MONTH RESULTS.

text.p: Financial services group ING Groep NV (ING) earlier announced a 24 percent increase in net profit to 2.34 billion guilders for the first nine months of 1996. Below is a selection of analysts' preliminary comments.

"We were expecting 2.27 billion. We weren't expecting banking to be quite as good as it was. There seems to be very strong lending growth helping interest income quite substantially. The commission income seems to be doing very well as well. Expenses seem to be quite high as well, so clearly there's a general expansion of the banking business, because expenses were a bit higher than we were going for."

"Our full year growth for net income at the moment is 15 percent, with 10 percent EPS growth. We might have to be edging that up a bit -- we could be perhaps going for 18 percent net income growth, which would mean 12-13 percent EPS growth."

"I don't have the details yet, but (the profit figure) was in line with market expectations, although perhaps a little lower than my expectations. A 25 percent profit increase is very high. (In the) longer-term, the next five years, it will probably be around 12 percent."
"(Investment bank) Barings last year was not very profitable. After interest charges, there was a loss. But this year it is making a profit for the banking side."

"They were very much in line with expectations. The insurance and the banking activities showed healthy growth, in spite of substantial extra costs. The insurance result was pressured by an extra charge of 150 million guilders set aside for automatisation, while 125 million guilders was taken off from the banking results for automatisation and auditing charges."
"I might revise my estimates of earnings per share for the whole of 1996, now at 4.39 guilders, slightly upwards. ING is always very cautious on their earnings forecasts."

"The premium income on life insurance was much higher than in the first half. Premium income rose 10 pct during the first nine months, while the increase during the first half amounted to only five percent. It seems very positive, but I wonder what type of products were sold. The third quarter (financial transactions) results equalled 1995. Apparently, the leaving of personnel at Barings has not had a very negative influence."
